study type: Mixed-methods study (observational human cohort and experimental animal model)
outcome: GBS colonization in infant intestinal tract
Relative abundance of GBS in infant stool
Translocation of GBS beyond the intestine (murine model)
cohort: The human cohort comprised prematurely born neonates from whom stool and maternal milk samples were collected, supplemented by a preclinical murine model of GBS infection.
finding: Maternal IgA concentration in milk negatively correlated with the relative abundance of GBS in infant stool, and maternal vaccination in a murine model induced strong immunoglobulin responses, including IgA, which reduced GBS intestinal colonization and mortality.
mod_finding: GBS intestinal colonization in neonates was not associated with delivery route.
